# pantechdynamics_load_balancer (Data Source)

Looks up one existing load balancer by id or name, to read its address, port or targets without managing it. Failed and deleted load balancers are not found.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Look an existing load balancer up by name (or by id). Names are not unique:
# if several share the name, the lookup fails and lists their ids.
data "pantechdynamics_load_balancer" "web" {
  name = "web"
}

output "web_address" {
  value = "${data.pantechdynamics_load_balancer.web.public_ip_address}:${data.pantechdynamics_load_balancer.web.public_port}"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Id of the load balancer to look up, starting with lb_. Set exactly one of id and name.
- `name` (String) Name of the load balancer to look up. It must match exactly. Names are not unique on the platform: if more than one load balancer has the name, the lookup fails and lists their ids. Set exactly one of id and name.

### Read-Only

- `algorithm` (String) How connections are spread: "roundrobin", "leastconn" or "source".
- `cidr_list` (Set of String) Source CIDRs allowed to connect. Empty allows any source.
- `created_at` (String) When the load balancer was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `instance_ids` (Set of String) Ids of the target instances, leaving out any being removed.
- `network_id` (String) Id of the VPC network the load balancer is in.
- `observed_state` (String) State of the load balancer as the platform sees it, for example "active".
- `private_port` (Number) Port on each target.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol balanced. Always "tcp".
- `public_ip_address` (String) The public IPv4 address clients connect to.
- `public_ip_id` (String) Id of the public IP clients connect to.
- `public_port` (Number) TCP port clients connect to.
- `subnet_id` (String) Id of the subnet the targets are in.
